Hi Elena & Jason — great call earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so your engineers can validate the sandbox end-to-end this week. I copied Dylan and Dev on the technical side.

What we agreed (high level)
- Goal: get a local dev sandbox that demonstrates generation + embeddings + reranker flow using your sample dataset; confirm auth and routing behavior for Dedicated vs Hosted.
- Success criteria: (1) run sample-app locally and call /generate -> streaming output works; (2) push ~10k embeddings to local FAISS test index and run reranker; (3) verify model routing header to dedicated pool.

Immediate next steps (owners & ETA)
- Lumina: confirm an engineer for pairing on Wed 11/24 (Elena/Jason)
- Redwood (Dev): provide a 15–30m pairing window + docker-compose that boots the sandbox with a stubbed reranker (Dev) — done in attachment runbook.
- Marissa: share runbook + quickstart snippets (this email + attachments) — done.

Auth options to try locally
- API key (fast): export REDWOOD_API_KEY and set REDWOOD_ENV=local. Example: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_xxx
- Service account (recommended for CI): use the JSON key and set REDWOOD_SA_KEY=/path/to/key.json; SDK will pick up RBAC scopes for embeddings/indexing.

Routing & model selection notes
- For Dedicated routing test, set HTTP header X-Redwood-Routing: dedicated:pool-1 or query param ?route=dedicated:pool-1. This will exercise the Dedicated path and metrics.
- For hosted fallbacks, use route=hosted:latest. Our runtime will fallback automatically if capacity isn't available.

Python quickstart (local)
- pip install redwood-inference
- from redwood import Client
- c = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'), host='http://localhost:8080')
- c.generate(model='gpt-lite-1', prompt='Write a 3-line summary', streaming=True)

TypeScript quickstart (local)
- npm i @redwood/inference
- import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference'
- const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, baseUrl: 'http://localhost:8080' })
- await client.generate({ model: 'gpt-lite-1', prompt: 'Summarize:' })

Embeddings & rerank flow (test plan)
- Use sample-apps/embedding-demo to create embeddings in batches of 256. Push into local FAISS index (we include a tiny FAISS container in the compose file).
- Call reranker: POST /rerank?model=rerank-v1 with top-N candidates; verify score ordering and latency under 150ms.

Attachments included
- redwood-sdk-sandbox-runbook.md — step-by-step runbook + docker-compose
- sample-apps.zip — minimal Python & TS apps for generation + embeddings
- lumina-mip-answers.pdf — answers to a few quick SOC/data residency queries you asked on the call

Questions for you (quick)
1) Which auth mode do you prefer for the pairing session — API key or service-account?
2) Do you have a preferred local port mapping (we default to 8080 for the runtime + 9200 for FAISS admin)?

I can be available for a short pairing block Wed 11/24 10–11am PT. If that works, reply with the engineer name and preferred auth mode and Dylan/Dev will prep the compose file for that mapping.

Elena — quick upsert curl + docker-compose that should match the runbook.

1) Embedding upsert (curl)
curl -X POST 'http://localhost:8080/v1/embeddings/upsert'
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '{"items": [{"id":"doc-1","text":"This is a test doc."}, {"id":"doc-2","text":"Second doc."}], "batch_size": 256}'

Response should return ids and vector sizes. You can then call /v1/embeddings/search with ?top_k=10 and confirm results.

2) Minimal docker-compose (excerpt)
version: '3.7'
services:
  runtime:
    image: redwood/runtime:local-202611
    ports:
      - '8080:8080'
    environment:
      - REDWOOD_ENV=local
      - REDWOOD_API_KEY=${REDWOOD_API_KEY}
  faiss:
    image: redwood/faiss-test:latest
    ports:
      - '9200:9200'
    volumes:
      - ./faiss-data:/data
  reranker-stub:
    image: redwood/reranker-stub:latest
    ports:
      - '9300:9300'

3) Python quick test (local)
from redwood import Client
import os
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'), base_url='http://localhost:8080')
# upsert embeddings
client.embeddings.upsert([{'id':'doc-1','text':'This is a test doc.'}])
# search
res = client.embeddings.search('test doc', top_k=10)
print(res)

4) Batch / performance tips
- Use batch_size=128–512 depending on token length. For short docs, 256 is a good starting point.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for repeated generate calls to reduce latency in the hosted path (REDWOOD_CACHE=true).
- For the reranker integration, our client has a rerank helper: client.rerank.score(candidates, query) — it uses a small HTTP payload and expects candidate ids returned by the embeddings search.

If you want, Dylan and I can post a short screencap (5–7m) showing a local run with the compose file next morning.
